verdict.rationale: jo's own docs say you can give it a recurring scheduled job, such as a weekly plan or morning priorities, "without asking each time." They also say it runs on an always-available per-user cloud machine that works overnight, so autonomous background runs are a first-party capability. The evidence is only marketing-level examples centred on briefings, so how far general-purpose automations go is unproven. Missing for 10: documentation of how automations are configured and managed (triggers beyond time schedules, editing, monitoring or logs), evidence of automations beyond briefing and planning use cases, and independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled jobs reliably run unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Give jo a job and a schedule. Get a weekly plan, morning priorities, or a weekend task review without asking each time.
because jo has its own machine, it can work overnight: read what came in, watch what changed, and prepare your morning before you wake.
Every user gets their own isolated cloud machine with its own storage.
